html:
Saint Patrick was a Romano-British missionary of the 400s who is credited with converting the Irish to Christianity. He is the patron saint of Ireland.

In his own short Confession he tells how raiders carried him off from Britain to Ireland as a teenager, where he herded sheep for six years before escaping. He later returned as a bishop and spent his life preaching, baptising and ordaining clergy, mostly in the north. His dates are uncertain.

Legends grew later: that he used the shamrock to explain the Trinity and drove the snakes from Ireland. The church he helped plant grew into the monastic world of the Book of Kells and of the Irish monks who carried learning across Europe. His feast, 17 March, is celebrated by the Irish around the world. See Christianity.
sum: Saint Patrick was a Romano-British missionary of the 400s who is credited with converting the Irish to Christianity. He is the patron saint of Ireland.
